main_text.l: Junctura femorum, &c. Id est, cingulum, quod est in ambi-
tu lumborum tuorum, æquat magnificentiam cujusvis mundi
muliebris, quantumvis affabrè facti & concinnati. Significat
autem cœlestis sponsus hac locutione desponsatam sibi Ecclesi-
am æque ornari omnium concupiscentiarum refrænatione, quâ
juxta principis Apostolorum præceptum 1 Pet. 1. v. 13. men-
tis nostræ lumbi succinguntur, atque mulier speciosa pretiosissi-
mis quibusque ornamentis & summo artificio factis.
Junctura. Heb. [illegible, ~5 letters], quam vocem interpretamur hic cin-
gulum, quo femora, seu lumbi præcinguntur & ambiuntur. De-
rivatur autem vox Hebraea à radice [illegible, ~3 letters], id est, circuivit.
Quia autem cinguli beneficio partes vestium in terram defluen-
tes cum iis, quæ corpus contegant, juxta femora conjungun-
tur, cingulum sponsæ potuit appellari Junctura femorum. Quin
& vox Hebraea [illegible, ~3 letters] non tantum femur sonat, sed & latus, pedem,

ornatum. Sæpe vox [illegible, ~3 letters] latiùs fumitur Arabicè, & in virorum

page.notes: The Hebrew and Arabic words in lines 2 and 3 of the commentary are printed in non-Latin script and are too small and damaged in the scan to read letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The final word "mirum" is set indented at the right end of the last line. The scan has a dark gutter shadow on the left and a dark crease through the centre of the last lines, which obscures part of "corporis est" and "prædicatorum".
